info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package crm is your sales pipeline: the companies, the people, the deals in play.

get.summary: ListApplications returns the org's Startup Program applications, newest first.
get.description:
ListApplications returns the org's Startup Program applications, newest first.
Each carries its AI screen and its stage history; a stage narrows the page to
one pipeline stage.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description:
Stage returns only the applications at that pipeline stage when set:
applied, screened, qualified, credits-offered, onboarded or rejected.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned: 200 by default, 1000 at most.

post.summary: Apply to the Startup Program from the public form
post.description:
Files an application to the Startup Program and answers the id and pipeline stage it landed at.

This is the ONE unauthenticated route in crm. It takes no principal and never reads a caller org: the application is filed against the DEPLOYMENT's own program org — the brand, hanzo unless white-labelled — so there is no tenant to name and none to leak. Reading the application back is staff-only and lives elsewhere.

company, contactName and a parseable email are required; everything else is optional context. Re-submitting the same (email, company) REFRESHES the existing application instead of filing a second one, so an impatient applicant cannot duplicate their own lead — that is a 200 where a first submission is a 201. A filled `hp` honeypot field is answered exactly like a success and stored nowhere, so a bot cannot tell a drop from an accept.

Filing is not screening: the application lands at stage `applied` with its AI screen still pending, and the screen runs afterwards on its own clock. A company and contact are also projected into the program org's ordinary CRM lists, best-effort — that projection failing does not fail the application. Bodies over 64 KiB are refused, and submissions are rate-limited.

get.summary: GetApplication returns one Startup Program application with its AI screen and stage history.
get.description:
GetApplication returns one Startup Program application with its AI screen and stage history.
An id belonging to another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, from the path.

patch.summary: PatchApplication moves one Startup Program application through the pipeline.
patch.description:
PatchApplication moves one Startup Program application through the pipeline. The
move is recorded on the application's timeline, attributed to the calling
staff user: it may advance exactly one stage, go back to any earlier stage,
reject from any non-rejected stage, or reopen a rejected application to
`applied`; anything else is refused. Rejecting requires a reason. A note with
no stage change is still recorded.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the application to move, from the path.

post.summary: CreateCompany adds a company to the caller's org and answers 201 with the stored record.
post.description:
CreateCompany adds a company to the caller's org and answers 201 with the stored record.
A name is required; an empty currency defaults to USD.

delete.summary: DeleteCompany removes one of the caller org's companies and answers 204.
delete.description:
DeleteCompany removes one of the caller org's companies and answers 204. Any
contact or opportunity in the org that referenced it keeps existing with the
reference cleared, so nothing is left pointing at a company that is gone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, from the path.

put.summary: UpdateCompany replaces one of the caller org's companies.
put.description:
UpdateCompany replaces one of the caller org's companies. Every writable
field is taken from the request, so a field the request omits is CLEARED —
send the whole record. A name is required.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID names the company to update and comes from the path. A create ignores
it: the server mints the id.

company.description: Company is the applicant's company name.

companyId.description:
CompanyID is the CRM Company minted for this lead at intake, so the startup
also appears in the org's standard CRM tabs. Empty when that best-effort
projection did not run.

contactId.description:
ContactID is the CRM Contact minted for this lead at intake. Empty when that
best-effort projection did not run.

contactName.description: ContactName is the person who applied.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the application arrived. Server-owned.

email.description:
Email is the applicant's email — half of the (email, company) key a
resubmission refreshes instead of duplicating.

events.description: Events is the append-only stage-transition log, oldest first.

id.description: ID is the server-minted application id ("appl_" + 128 random bits).

metadata.description:
Metadata is the FULL submitted form, every field, including the arrays the
promoted columns above do not carry (tier1Investors, useCases) and the
deterministic tier1Matched list.

reason.description:
Reason is why the application was rejected, required to reject. Empty
otherwise.

role.description: Role is the applicant's role at their company.

screen.description:
Screen is the AI screen. It runs after intake, so a freshly created
application carries a "pending" screen.

stage.description:
Stage is the pipeline stage: applied, screened, qualified, credits-offered,
onboarded or rejected. Server-owned — it starts at "applied" and moves only
through the transition machine.

tier1.description:
Tier1 is whether the applicant is tier-1 backed, derived deterministically
at intake from the submitted fund list — independent of the AI screen.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the unix second of the last write. Server-owned.

website.description: Website is the applicant's website as submitted.

arr.description: ARR is annual recurring revenue in minor units (cents) of Currency.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the company was created. Server-owned.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO code ARR is denominated in; a write that names none
stores USD.

domainName.description: DomainName is the company's primary domain, e.g. "acme.com".

id.description: ID is the server-minted company id ("comp_" + 128 random bits).

idealCustomerProfile.description: ICP marks the company as an ideal-customer-profile fit.

linkedinLink.description: Linkedin is the company's LinkedIn URL.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the unix second of the last write. Server-owned.

xLink.description: XLink is the company's X (Twitter) URL.

city.description: City is where the person is based.

companyId.description:
CompanyID links the contact to one of the org's companies; empty when the
contact stands alone, and cleared when its company is deleted. A write
naming a company the org does not own is refused with 422.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the contact was created. Server-owned.

email.description: Email is the person's email address.

firstName.description: FirstName is the person's given name.

id.description: ID is the server-minted contact id ("cont_" + 128 random bits).

jobTitle.description: JobTitle is the person's role at their company.

lastName.description: LastName is the person's family name.

linkedinLink.description: Linkedin is the person's LinkedIn URL.

phone.description: Phone is the person's phone number.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the unix second of the last write. Server-owned.

xLink.description: XLink is the person's X (Twitter) URL.

amount.description: Amount is the deal value in minor units (cents) of Currency.

closeDate.description: CloseDate is the expected close as a unix second (0 = unset).

companyId.description:
CompanyID links the deal to one of the org's companies; empty when
unlinked, and cleared when that company is deleted. A write naming a
company the org does not own is refused with 422.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the opportunity was created. Server-owned.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO code Amount is denominated in; a write that names none
stores USD.

id.description: ID is the server-minted opportunity id ("oppo_" + 128 random bits).

pointOfContactId.description:
PointOfContact links the deal to one of the org's contacts; empty when
unlinked, and cleared when that contact is deleted. A write naming a
contact the org does not own is refused with 422.

stage.description:
Stage is the pipeline stage, always one of NEW, SCREENING, MEETING,
PROPOSAL or CUSTOMER — stored upper-case whatever case the write used.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the unix second of the last write. Server-owned.

draftReply.description: DraftReply is a suggested email reply for staff to edit and send.

error.description:
Error says why a failed screen failed — no AI gateway configured, a gateway
error, or a reply that carried no parseable JSON. Absent on success.

model.description: Model is the LLM the screen ran on.

score.description: Score is the model's 0..100 fit score, clamped to that range.

screenedAt.description: ScreenedAt is the unix second the screen finished (0 while pending).

status.description: Status is the screen's state: pending | done | failed.

suggestedCredits.description:
SuggestedCredits is the recommended credit grant in USD, snapped to the
nearest allowed rung: 0 | 5000 | 25000 | 50000 | 150000.

summary.description: Summary is the model's short assessment of the application.

tier1Backed.description:
Tier1Backed is the model's read on tier-1 backing, normalized to
"yes", "no" or "unclear" (anything it cannot resolve reads "unclear").

at.description: At is the unix second of the move.

by.description:
By is who moved it: "system" for intake and the AI auto-advance, else the
validated staff user id.

from.description: From is the stage moved out of; empty on the intake event that opens the log.

note.description: Note is the free-text comment recorded with the move. Absent when none.

to.description: To is the stage moved into.

data.description: Data is the page of applications, newest first.

companyId.description: CompanyID links the deal to one of the org's companies.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO code Amount is denominated in; empty defaults to USD.

stage.description:
